examples.hard: It's strange that my best friend and I were born on the same day in the same hospital.

examples.normal: My sister and I have very different hobbies.
examples.hard: People in different parts of the country have different traditions for weddings and holidays.

examples.normal: We spent the whole day at the beach.
examples.hard: The whole family came to the airport to say goodbye when my brother left to study abroad.

examples.normal: Can you cut the cake into eight pieces?
examples.hard: Be careful when you cut onions with that knife, because it is very sharp.

examples.normal: We had a lovely time at your party, thank you.
examples.hard: The hotel had a lovely view of the sea, and we watched the sun go down from our balcony every evening.

examples.normal: Don't worry about the money; you can pay me later.
examples.hard: Don't worry if you make mistakes when you speak, because that's how everyone learns a new language.

examples.normal: Take a cardigan with you; it might get cold later.
examples.hard: My grandmother knitted me a warm wool cardigan with wooden buttons for my birthday.

examples.normal: These trousers are too big, so I have to wear a belt.
examples.hard: He bought a brown leather belt to match his shoes for his cousin's wedding.

examples.normal: I need to buy some new tights for work.
examples.hard: In winter she wears thick wool tights under her skirt to keep her legs warm.

examples.normal: My son always wears his baseball cap backwards.
examples.hard: Wear a cap when you go out in the midday sun, or you might get a headache.

examples.normal: The teacher gave us a worksheet with twenty grammar exercises.
examples.hard: Complete the worksheet at home and bring it to the next lesson, so that we can check the answers together.

examples.normal: I always wear a thick jumper when I go walking in winter.
examples.hard: My mother told me to put on a jumper because the evenings in the mountains get cold very quickly.

examples.normal: He bought a pair of black trousers for his new job.
examples.hard: My trousers got wet when I was caught in the rain, so I had to change before the meeting.

examples.normal: He wears colourful socks with his work suit.
examples.hard: I bought a pack of thick socks for our trip, because the nights in the mountains are very cold.

examples.normal: These shoes are too small; I need a bigger size.
examples.hard: It's a good idea to wear comfortable shoes when you visit the old city, because the streets are made of stone.

examples.easy: I wear training shoes for running.
examples.normal: He bought new training shoes before the city marathon.
examples.hard: Good training shoes are expensive, but they protect your knees and feet if you run every day.

examples.normal: Hurry up and get dressed, or we'll be late for school.
examples.hard: It takes my daughter almost half an hour to get dressed, because she can never decide what to wear.

examples.easy: The children get undressed for bed.
examples.normal: He got undressed and went straight to bed after the long journey.
examples.hard: The doctor asked him to get undressed to the waist so that she could listen to his chest.

examples.normal: It's very windy, so button up your jacket before you go out.
examples.hard: My son is only four, but he can already button up his shirt by himself without any help.

examples.normal: He unbuttoned his collar because the room was so hot.
examples.hard: The doctor asked me to unbutton my shirt so that she could listen to my heart.

examples.normal: She has short hair and big brown eyes.
examples.hard: My trousers are too short now, because I have grown a lot since last summer.

examples.normal: This dress is too long; I need to shorten it.
examples.hard: The giraffe has a very long neck, so it can eat leaves from the tops of tall trees.

examples.normal: Your jacket is creased; did you sleep in it?
examples.hard: After the long flight, all the clothes in my suitcase were creased, so I had to iron them at the hotel.

examples.normal: I always wear a clean, ironed shirt to work.
examples.hard: She laid out her freshly ironed clothes on the bed the night before her important job interview.

examples.normal: Don't forget to take the price tag off the present.
examples.hard: I loved the coat, but when I saw the price tag, I decided it was much too expensive for me.

examples.normal: Close your books and listen to me, please.
examples.hard: Please close all the windows before you leave, because it's going to rain this afternoon.

examples.normal: Do you remember the name of that little restaurant?
examples.hard: I remember the day we moved into this house, because it was snowing and the car broke down.

examples.normal: My mother made a chocolate birthday cake for me.
examples.hard: We put eight candles on my son's birthday cake, and he blew them all out at once.

examples.normal: We decorated the classroom with balloons for the party.
examples.hard: Every year the children decorate the house with lights and paper flowers before the New Year celebrations.

examples.normal: The bad weather spoilt our day at the beach.
examples.hard: Don't tell me how the film ends, because you'll spoil it for me before I've had a chance to see it.

examples.normal: Nobody listens to him, because he is a bigot.
examples.hard: He was a bigot who refused to work with anyone from a different religion or background.

examples.easy: There is blood on his shirt.
examples.normal: The nurse took some blood from my arm for a test.
examples.hard: Giving blood is quick and safe, and it can help to save the lives of people after accidents.

examples.normal: It's hard to breathe in this hot, crowded room.
examples.hard: The doctor told me to breathe in deeply and hold my breath while she listened to my chest.

examples.normal: We had bad luck with the weather on our holiday.
examples.hard: With a bit of luck, we'll get to the station before the last train leaves.

examples.easy: Exercise is good for your body.
examples.normal: Drinking enough water helps your body to work properly.
examples.hard: After the long walk in the mountains, every part of my body hurt, but I felt very happy.

examples.normal: She sang a beautiful song at her sister's wedding.
examples.hard: Every time I hear that old song on the radio, I remember the summer we spent at my grandparents' house.

examples.normal: Do you know where the nearest bank is?
examples.hard: I've known my best friend since we were six, and we still meet every week for coffee.

examples.normal: My children don't like to eat vegetables.
examples.hard: We usually eat out on Fridays, because nobody wants to cook at the end of a long week.

examples.normal: Someone is knocking at the front door.
examples.hard: Please lock the back door before you go to bed, because there have been some burglaries in the area.

examples.normal: We need more chairs for the guests.
examples.hard: You need a visa to visit that country, so apply for one at least a month before you travel.

examples.easy: I would like a coffee, please.
examples.normal: Would you like to come to dinner on Saturday?
examples.hard: I would like to book a table for four people at eight o'clock tomorrow evening, please.

examples.normal: There is a satellite dish on almost every balcony in our street.
examples.hard: After the storm, the satellite dish fell off the roof, so we couldn't watch the football match.

examples.easy: Smoke comes out of the chimney.
examples.normal: There is a bird's nest in our old chimney.
examples.hard: In winter, you can see smoke rising from the chimneys of every house in the village.

examples.normal: The rain is coming through a hole in the roof.
examples.hard: We need to repair the roof before winter, because last year water came into the bedroom.

examples.easy: The car is in the garage.
examples.normal: My father keeps his tools in the garage.
examples.hard: We turned our old garage into a small workshop where my husband repairs furniture.

examples.normal: Ring the bell and wait for someone to open the door.
examples.hard: When the bell rang at the end of the lesson, all the children ran outside to play in the yard.

examples.easy: The dog is in its kennel.
examples.normal: My father built a wooden kennel for our dog.
examples.hard: We leave our dog at a kennel near the airport whenever we go away on holiday.

examples.normal: She was sitting on the front steps, waiting for her friend.
examples.hard: The museum has a lot of steep steps at the entrance, so it is difficult for older visitors.

examples.normal: Our dog jumped over the fence and ran into the street.
examples.hard: We built a high wooden fence around the garden, so that our neighbours can't see in.

examples.normal: Beethoven wrote nine symphonies.
examples.hard: The orchestra played Tchaikovsky's sixth symphony, and the audience stood up and clapped for several minutes.

examples.easy: Don't lean out of the window!
examples.normal: It is dangerous to lean out of the train window.
examples.hard: The old woman leaned out of her window to see what all the noise in the street was about.

examples.normal: Quantifiers like "much" and "many" tell us how much of something there is.
examples.hard: We use the quantifier "much" with uncountable nouns and "many" with countable nouns in questions.

examples.normal: My mother always worries when I travel alone.
examples.hard: There is no need to worry about the exam, because you have been studying hard for months.

examples.easy: This table is made of wood.
examples.normal: We need more wood for the fire tonight.
examples.hard: My grandfather loves working with wood, and he made all the furniture in our kitchen himself.

examples.normal: My mother makes pancakes for breakfast on Sundays.
examples.hard: In Britain, people eat pancakes with lemon and sugar on a special day in February called Pancake Day.

examples.normal: I always have a cup of coffee before I start work.
examples.hard: Before you sign the contract, read it carefully and ask questions about anything you don't understand.

examples.easy: Please continue reading after the break.
examples.normal: After a short break, the teacher continued the lesson.
examples.hard: Although it started to rain heavily, the players continued the match until the referee stopped it.

examples.normal: You need a bank account to get your salary.
examples.hard: She opened a bank account for her son, so that he could start saving money for university.

examples.normal: During buzzing time, students talk to their partners about the task.
examples.hard: The teacher gave us five minutes of buzzing time to share our ideas with a partner before the class discussion.

examples.normal: How much sugar do you take in your tea?
examples.hard: How much money do you think we will need for a week's holiday by the sea?

examples.easy: How many children do you have?
examples.normal: How many people are coming to the meeting?
examples.hard: How many languages do you need to speak to get a job at an international company?

examples.easy: This trip is a great opportunity to practise English.
examples.normal: The new job gave her the opportunity to travel abroad.
examples.hard: Studying abroad was a wonderful opportunity to learn a new language and meet people from many countries.

examples.normal: There are many wild animals in this forest.
examples.hard: The forest near our village is beautiful in autumn, when the leaves turn yellow and red.

examples.easy: We are going to wallpaper the room.
examples.normal: My father wallpapered the bedroom in one weekend.
examples.hard: Before you wallpaper the walls, make sure they are clean and dry, or the paper will not stick properly.

examples.normal: The two villages are very close together.
examples.hard: The trees were planted too close together, so some of them did not get enough sunlight to grow.

examples.normal: The two cities are very far apart.
examples.hard: My children live far apart from each other, so it is hard for the whole family to meet more than once a year.

examples.easy: Would you like a glass of wine?
examples.normal: We had a bottle of red wine with our dinner.
examples.hard: This region is famous for its wine, and tourists come every autumn to visit the vineyards.

examples.normal: Cigarettes are very bad for your health.
examples.hard: My uncle stopped smoking cigarettes ten years ago, and now he feels much healthier.

examples.easy: Put some oil in the pan.
examples.normal: We cook with sunflower oil in our house.
examples.hard: Heat a little oil in a large pan, then add the onions and cook them until they are soft.

examples.easy: Our classroom is on the second floor.
examples.normal: There are twenty desks in our classroom.
examples.hard: The new classroom has a big interactive board, so the teacher can show videos during the lesson.

examples.normal: We picked mushrooms in the forest last weekend.
examples.hard: Don't eat wild mushrooms unless you know they are safe, because some of them are very poisonous.

examples.normal: My son always orders a hamburger and chips.
examples.hard: Eating hamburgers every day is not healthy, because they usually contain a lot of fat and salt.

examples.normal: Could you pass me that book on the table?
examples.hard: At dinner my grandfather asked me to pass him the bread, but I gave him the salt by mistake.

examples.normal: We bought some furniture for our new flat.
examples.hard: All the furniture in this room is made of wood, and most of it belonged to my grandparents.

examples.normal: We had chicken with rice and peas for dinner.
examples.hard: Fresh green peas from the garden taste so sweet that the children eat them straight from the pod.

examples.normal: It's necessary to book a table at that restaurant.
examples.hard: It isn't necessary to bring food to the party, but you can bring some drinks if you like.

examples.normal: How much milk is there in the fridge?
examples.hard: We didn't spend much money on our holiday, because we stayed with friends and cooked our own meals.

examples.normal: How many brothers and sisters do you have?
examples.hard: There weren't many tourists in the city in winter, so we could visit the museums without waiting.

examples.easy: I have a lot of friends.
examples.normal: There is a lot of traffic in the city centre today.
examples.hard: We have a lot of work to do before the end of the month, so nobody can take a holiday now.

examples.normal: We had lots of fun at the party last night.
examples.hard: My grandmother has lots of old photos, and she loves telling us the stories behind each of them.

examples.normal: Can you buy some cheese for the sandwiches?
examples.hard: This cheese comes from a small farm in the mountains, where it is made from fresh goat's milk.

examples.easy: He drinks a beer after work.
examples.normal: Would you like a beer or a soft drink?
examples.hard: The brewery in our town makes a light beer that is popular with tourists in summer.

examples.easy: The next session starts at ten.
examples.normal: Our training session lasts two hours.
examples.hard: The evening session was very useful, because the teacher answered all our questions about the exam.

examples.easy: I'm tired because I worked late.
examples.normal: We stayed at home because it was raining.
examples.hard: She decided to study medicine because she wanted to help people in her village who couldn't see a doctor.

examples.normal: After the trip, we had to stay in quarantine for two weeks.
examples.hard: During the quarantine, schools were closed and many people had to work from home for several months.

examples.normal: We are having lunch now, can I call you back?
examples.hard: Right now the company is looking for new staff, so it's a good time to send them your CV.

examples.normal: There is very little water in the desert.
examples.hard: Travelling across the desert by camel was an amazing experience, but the nights were surprisingly cold.

examples.easy: The children play in the sand.
examples.normal: My shoes are full of sand after the walk on the beach.
examples.hard: The strong wind blew sand into our eyes, so we had to cover our faces with scarves.

examples.easy: I buy fruit at the market.
examples.normal: The market is open every day except Monday.
examples.hard: Chorsu Bazaar is one of the oldest markets in Tashkent, and you can buy almost anything there.

examples.normal: Be careful when you cross the road.
examples.hard: Be careful with that knife, because it's very sharp and you could easily cut yourself.

examples.normal: The Sahara is in the north of Africa.
examples.hard: The Sahara is the largest hot desert in the world, and it covers parts of more than ten countries.

examples.normal: Prices go up every year.
examples.hard: We went up to the top of the tower, and from there we could see the whole city.

examples.normal: The temperature goes down at night in the desert.
examples.hard: After the storm, the river went down, and people could finally return to their homes.

examples.easy: Can I give you some advice?
examples.normal: My father gave me some good advice about money.
examples.hard: If you need advice about your visa, you should speak to someone at the embassy before you travel.

examples.normal: Put some butter in the pan before you add the eggs.
examples.hard: This cake recipe needs two hundred grams of butter, three eggs and a cup of sugar.

units.name: Lesson 13 - Present continuous and daily actions

examples.normal: We both like football, so we often watch matches together.
examples.hard: Both of my parents worked long hours, but they always found time to help us with homework.

examples.normal: Every English sentence needs a verb, like 'go' or 'have'.
examples.hard: In the present continuous, we add -ing to the main verb and use 'am', 'is' or 'are'.

examples.easy: At present, I live in Tashkent.
examples.normal: At present, my brother is working as a driver in Moscow.
examples.hard: At present, the company is looking for new staff, so they are interviewing people every week.

examples.normal: Can you call me back later? I'm driving now.
examples.hard: My grandmother is ninety now, but she still walks to the market every morning by herself.

examples.easy: She is sleeping at the moment.
examples.normal: I'm sorry, the manager is in a meeting at the moment.
examples.hard: At the moment we are renting a small flat, but we hope to buy a house next year.

examples.normal: We usually sit in the garden after dinner in summer.
examples.hard: The old man was sitting on the bench, feeding the birds and watching the children play.

examples.normal: We had to stand on the bus because it was full.
examples.hard: The students stood up when the teacher came in, and nobody sat down until she smiled.

examples.normal: I usually wear a warm coat and boots in winter.
examples.hard: You don't need to wear a tie at our office, but most people still dress quite smartly.

examples.easy: The bus stops in front of school.
examples.normal: There is a big tree in front of our building.
examples.hard: I felt nervous when I had to speak in front of three hundred people at the conference.

examples.easy: He is wearing a black suit.
examples.normal: My father bought a new suit for my sister's wedding.
examples.hard: If you have a job interview at a bank, it's a good idea to wear a dark suit.

examples.easy: I have a dog called Max.
examples.normal: We stayed at a small hotel called The Green House.
examples.hard: She is reading a novel called 'The Kite Runner', which her teacher recommended to the whole class.

examples.easy: How do you spell your name?
examples.normal: Could you spell your surname for me, please? Thank you.
examples.hard: Many learners find English hard to spell because words are often not written the way they sound.

examples.normal: The cat likes to lie in the sun all afternoon.
examples.hard: After the long walk, she was lying on the sofa, too tired to make dinner.

examples.normal: His grandfather died when he was eighty-five years old.
examples.hard: Many fish are dying in the river because a factory is putting chemicals into the water.

examples.easy: I love the sound of rain.
examples.normal: Can you hear that strange sound coming from the kitchen?
examples.hard: The sound of the traffic outside kept me awake most of the night, so I'm exhausted today.

examples.normal: Please keep your phones silent during the lesson.
examples.hard: Everyone went silent when the director walked into the room with the results of the exam.

examples.normal: Do you have a pen I can borrow for a minute?
examples.hard: We have a small house in the village, and we spend most summer weekends there with our children.

examples.normal: It was my first time on an airplane, and I was nervous.
examples.hard: The airplane was delayed for three hours because of the snow, so we missed our connecting flight.

examples.easy: I wrote a letter to Grandma.
examples.normal: She received a letter from the university this morning.
examples.hard: Before mobile phones, my parents wrote long letters to each other every week while he was in the army.

examples.normal: My cousin is studying medicine at a university in Samarkand.
examples.hard: If you study a little every day, you'll remember more than if you cram before exams.

examples.easy: I watch this programme every Sunday.
examples.normal: There is a good cooking programme on TV tonight at eight.
examples.hard: The new training programme helps unemployed people learn computer skills and find jobs in just six months.

examples.easy: I listen to music at night.
examples.normal: What kind of music do you like listening to in the car?
examples.hard: She has been playing music since she was six, and now she teaches piano at a local school.

examples.easy: Would you like a cup of tea?
examples.normal: I always have a cup of tea with breakfast before work.
examples.hard: Whenever guests come to our house, my mother makes a cup of tea and puts sweets on the table.

examples.normal: Please don't throw your rubbish on the street or in the park.
examples.hard: The boys were throwing stones into the lake, trying to see who could throw the furthest.

examples.normal: If you misbehave again, you can't play computer games tonight.
examples.hard: The teacher called his parents because he had been misbehaving in lessons for several weeks.

examples.normal: We always sing songs together at family celebrations.
examples.hard: My grandfather used to sing old folk songs while he was working in the garden.

examples.normal: Let's invite your parents for dinner on Saturday evening.
examples.hard: By the time I got home from work, my family had already finished dinner and washed the dishes.

examples.normal: My grandfather made this wooden table with his own hands.
examples.hard: The children are making birthday cards for their mother while she is out at the shops.

examples.normal: It often snows in the mountains in December and January.
examples.hard: It snowed so heavily last night that the schools were closed and nobody could drive to work.

examples.normal: My uncle goes to the mountains to hunt every autumn.
examples.hard: Lions usually hunt in groups, and the females do most of the work while the males rest.

examples.easy: Can you come to my party?
examples.normal: My friends are coming to our house for dinner tonight.
examples.hard: When I come home late, my mother always waits for me in the kitchen with a hot meal.

examples.normal: Don't eat too much candy, or you'll have problems with your teeth.
examples.hard: In America, children dress up on Halloween and go from house to house asking for candy.

examples.normal: She wrote a beautiful song for her mother's birthday.
examples.hard: Whenever I hear this song on the radio, I remember the summer we spent at the seaside.

examples.normal: With a one syllable verb like 'sit', double the last letter.
examples.hard: Remember that with a short one syllable verb like 'swim', you double the final consonant: 'swimming'.

examples.normal: Take an umbrella; it's going to rain this afternoon.
examples.hard: It had been raining for three days, so the river was much higher than usual.

examples.normal: My grandmother drinks green tea after every meal.
examples.hard: Doctors say you should drink at least two litres of water a day, especially in hot weather.

examples.normal: I wish I could speak English as well as you do.
examples.hard: My colleagues wished me luck before my interview, and their kind words really helped me relax.

examples.normal: We have three kids, two boys and a girl.
examples.hard: When I was a kid, we didn't have smartphones, so we played football in the street all day.

examples.easy: We moved to a new flat.
examples.normal: My sister is moving to London next month for work.
examples.hard: After living in the same house for twenty years, my parents decided to move to a smaller flat.

examples.normal: He runs five kilometres every morning before breakfast.
examples.hard: I was running to catch the bus when I slipped on the ice and hurt my knee.

examples.normal: Where did you get that nice jacket? It looks great.
examples.hard: She got a lot of presents for her birthday, but her favourite was a book from her grandfather.

examples.normal: They are planning a big party for their parents' anniversary.
examples.hard: We planned our holiday very carefully, but the weather was so bad that we stayed inside most days.

examples.normal: You need to spend more time with your children.
examples.hard: Now that I work from home, I have more free time, but I also feel more lonely.

examples.normal: I began learning English when I was twelve years old.
examples.hard: The concert was supposed to begin at seven, but it didn't start until almost eight o'clock.

examples.normal: Can you tell me the way to the station, please?
examples.hard: My grandmother used to tell us stories about her childhood in the village before we went to sleep.

examples.normal: She regrets not studying harder when she was at school.
examples.hard: I will always regret that I didn't visit my grandfather more often before he became ill.

examples.normal: She finally admitted that she had broken the window.
examples.hard: It took him a long time to admit that he needed help with his studies.

examples.normal: He was upset because nobody remembered his birthday.
examples.hard: My mother gets upset when we forget to call her, so I try to phone her every evening.

examples.normal: This is the last bus, so we mustn't miss it.
examples.hard: Last summer we visited Bukhara, and it was the most interesting trip we have ever taken.

examples.normal: Some verbs have spelling changes when you add -ing to them.
examples.hard: Spelling changes like 'make' to 'making' confuse many learners, so we practise them in every lesson.

examples.normal: Our teacher explained the spelling rules for adding -ing.
examples.hard: Even native speakers sometimes forget the spelling rules, so don't worry if you make a few mistakes.

examples.normal: She tied her hair back before she started cooking.
examples.hard: Before the storm, the fishermen tied their boats to the wall so the wind couldn't carry them away.

examples.easy: Please set the table for dinner.
examples.normal: The children help me set the table every evening.
examples.hard: While my husband was cooking, I set the table with our best plates because his parents were coming.

examples.normal: My father taught me how to ride a bike.
examples.hard: He has been teaching mathematics for thirty years, and many of his students have become engineers.

examples.normal: The manager dictated a letter, and his secretary typed it.
examples.hard: Every Monday our teacher dictates a short text, and we have to write it down without mistakes.

examples.normal: It's ten o'clock, and my son is still sleeping.
examples.hard: Although she moved to Canada twenty years ago, she still cooks plov every Friday for her family.

examples.normal: Please type your password again and then press 'Enter'.
examples.hard: She learnt to type with ten fingers when she was a secretary, and now she never looks at the keyboard.

examples.normal: The sun was shining, so we had lunch in the garden.
examples.hard: When the sun shines through the window in the morning, the whole kitchen looks warm and bright.

examples.normal: I read about the new metro station in the local newspaper.
examples.hard: Fewer people buy a newspaper these days because they can read the news on their phones for free.

examples.normal: Many families in Europe eat chocolate eggs at Easter.
examples.hard: Easter is an important holiday for Christians, and in Britain many shops close on Easter Sunday.

examples.normal: My uncle always tells jokes at big family dinners.
examples.hard: I didn't understand the joke at first, but everyone else was laughing so much that I started laughing too.

examples.normal: The baby smiled when she saw her grandmother's face.
examples.hard: Smile when you answer the phone, because people can actually hear it in your voice.

examples.normal: Please stop talking and listen to the instructions.
examples.hard: It finally stopped raining, so we put on our boots and went for a long walk.

examples.normal: Our neighbour's dog barks every time someone walks past.
examples.hard: The dog started barking loudly when the postman opened the gate, and it woke up the whole family.

examples.normal: They celebrated their wedding anniversary at a nice restaurant.
examples.hard: After she passed her driving test, we celebrated with a big dinner and a chocolate cake.

examples.normal: She is preparing for her English exam next week.
examples.hard: My mother spent the whole day preparing food for the guests who were coming in the evening.

examples.normal: The police chased the thief through the busy market.
examples.hard: The children were chasing each other around the garden, laughing and shouting until it got dark.

examples.normal: I usually sleep for seven hours on weekdays.
examples.hard: I couldn't sleep last night because the neighbours were having a noisy party until three.

examples.normal: My grandmother bakes the best apple cake in the family.
examples.hard: She has been baking cakes for weddings and birthdays since she lost her office job last year.

examples.normal: Would you like another piece of pie with your tea?
examples.hard: My mother bakes a meat pie every Sunday, and the smell fills the whole house.

examples.normal: My uncle keeps chickens and two turkeys on his farm.
examples.hard: In the USA, most families eat roast turkey on Thanksgiving Day, which is in late November.

examples.normal: Please don't walk on the grass in the park.
examples.hard: We sat on the grass under a big tree and had a picnic while the children played football.

examples.normal: We waited for you for an hour at the café.
examples.hard: She was waiting for the results of her exam, so she couldn't think about anything else.

examples.normal: My grandfather told us a funny story about his army days.
examples.hard: The story of how my parents met is so romantic that everyone asks them to tell it again.

examples.easy: I often think about my future.
examples.normal: Nobody knows what the future will bring for our children.
examples.hard: In the future, I'd like to open my own small business and work for myself.

examples.easy: We have an arrangement with them.
examples.normal: I've made arrangements to meet my cousin at the airport.
examples.hard: We use the present continuous for fixed arrangements, like 'I'm meeting Anna on Friday at six.'

examples.normal: Tomorrow I'm visiting my grandparents in the village.
examples.hard: I can't come to the cinema tomorrow because I'm working late and then going to the gym.

examples.normal: My tooth hurts, so I need to go to the dentist.
examples.hard: I'm going to the dentist on Thursday because one of my back teeth has been hurting for days.

examples.easy: I can see my friend at the bus stop.
examples.normal: Did you see the football match on TV last night?
examples.hard: From the top floor of the hotel, you can see the whole city and the river.

examples.normal: Last year we visited Istanbul for the first time.
examples.hard: If you visit Samarkand, don't miss Registan Square, especially in the evening when it is lit up.

examples.normal: The shop is closed on Mondays, so let's go on Tuesday.

examples.normal: We're going away for the weekend to visit my parents.

examples.normal: Our neighbours have a big ginger cat called Tiger.

examples.normal: I usually take a short nap after lunch on Sundays.

examples.normal: My husband has to wear a suit and tie to work.
examples.hard: I bought my father a silk tie for his birthday, but he says he only wears one at weddings.

examples.normal: Ahmed is a very common name in our country.
examples.hard: Back pain is very common among office workers who sit at a computer all day.

examples.easy: I drink tea instead of coffee.

examples.hard: Instead of spending all her money on clothes, she decided to save it for a trip abroad.

examples.normal: We swam in the sea every day of our holiday.

examples.normal: He lit the candles on the cake with a lighter.

examples.easy: There's a globe on my desk.

examples.hard: My son loves spinning the globe and asking me about the countries and oceans he finds on it.

examples.normal: Can you show me how to use the new photocopier?
examples.hard: There is a long queue at the photocopier every morning because all the teachers need copies for their lessons.

examples.normal: She wrote the new words on the board with white chalk.
examples.hard: Most schools now use whiteboards and markers, but some old classrooms still have blackboards and chalk.

examples.normal: Please clean the board with the board rubber after class.

examples.normal: She cut out an interesting article from the newspaper.

examples.normal: Put a paper clip on these pages so they don't get lost.
examples.hard: She kept all her receipts together with a paper clip so she could give them to the accountant.

examples.normal: All the reports for this month are in the blue folder.
examples.hard: I keep my passport, birth certificate and other important papers in a plastic folder in the drawer.

examples.normal: Please bring all the necessary documents to the interview.
examples.hard: It isn't necessary to book a table on weekdays, but at the weekend the restaurant is always full.

examples.normal: I have an important meeting with my boss at ten.
examples.hard: It is important to drink enough water, especially when you exercise on a hot summer day.

examples.normal: The manager gave an order to close the shop early.
examples.hard: The workers refused to follow the new orders because they thought the rules were unfair.

examples.normal: Don't worry, there is plenty of food for everyone tonight.
examples.hard: Make sure you get plenty of sleep before the exam, or you won't be able to concentrate.

examples.normal: I like this shirt, but do you have it in other colours?
examples.hard: Some people prefer to work alone, while other people work much better in a team.

examples.normal: My parents forbid me to stay out after ten o'clock.
examples.hard: The new law forbids drivers to use their mobile phones while they are driving in the city.

examples.normal: Check your visa, because it might expire before your trip ends.
examples.hard: I couldn't use my credit card in the shop because it had expired at the end of last month.

examples.normal: It took three weeks to get a visa for the UK.
examples.hard: You should apply for a student visa at least two months before your course in Germany begins.

examples.easy: Hurry up, otherwise we'll be late.
examples.normal: Take an umbrella, otherwise you will get wet in the rain.
examples.hard: You must save your work every few minutes, otherwise you could lose everything if the computer crashes.

examples.easy: The penalty is a big fine.
examples.normal: There is a heavy penalty for parking in this street.
examples.hard: In many countries the penalty for driving after drinking alcohol is losing your licence for a year.

examples.normal: This room is too small. Can we see another one?
examples.hard: We didn't have time to visit the old city, so we'll have to come back another time.

examples.normal: I had a strange feeling that someone was watching me.
examples.hard: It's not easy to talk about your feelings, but it often helps to share them with a close friend.

examples.normal: The hotel room was small but clean and very comfortable.
examples.hard: I prefer to travel by train because the seats are more comfortable and I can read on the way.

examples.normal: My grandmother grows vegetables like carrots and tomatoes in her garden.
examples.hard: Doctors say we should eat at least five portions of fruit and vegetables every day to stay healthy.

examples.normal: She fastened her coat because it was cold and windy outside.
examples.hard: Passengers must keep their seatbelts fastened until the plane has completely stopped at the gate.

examples.normal: I overslept and missed the first bus to work this morning.
examples.hard: My alarm clock didn't go off, so I overslept and arrived at the airport just before the check-in closed.

examples.normal: When she lost her passport at the airport, she started to panic.
examples.hard: People began to panic when the lights went out, but the staff calmly led everyone out of the building.

examples.normal: He lives with his father and his stepmother in Samarkand.
examples.hard: After her parents divorced, she found it difficult to get on with her new stepmother at first.

examples.normal: She has been divorced for five years and lives alone now.
examples.hard: They got divorced after ten years of marriage, but they are still good friends and share the children.

examples.normal: Breakfast is the most important meal of the day for me.
examples.hard: We booked a table at a nice restaurant to have a special meal for our wedding anniversary.

examples.normal: I could see from his face that he was telling a lie.
examples.hard: She was punished at school for telling a lie about why she hadn't done her homework.

examples.normal: My husband usually cooks dinner when I work late.
examples.hard: She met her husband at university, and they got married a year after they both graduated.

examples.normal: His wife works as a nurse at the city hospital.
examples.hard: He bought his wife a beautiful necklace for their tenth wedding anniversary last month.

examples.normal: Our son wants to study medicine at university next year.
examples.hard: Their eldest son lives in Tashkent, but the younger one moved abroad to work as an engineer.

examples.normal: I bought a birthday present for my niece yesterday afternoon.
examples.hard: My sister's daughter is my only niece, and she often stays with us during the school holidays.

examples.normal: All our relatives came to the wedding from different cities.
examples.hard: During the holidays we always visit our relatives in the village and stay with them for a week.

examples.normal: He was the only person in the office who spoke Japanese.
examples.hard: As the only doctor in the village, she works very long hours and rarely takes a day off.

examples.normal: It's quite cold today, so take a warm jacket with you.
examples.hard: The exam was quite difficult, but I think I answered most of the questions correctly.

examples.normal: He couldn't sleep all night because of a terrible toothache.
examples.hard: If you eat too many sweets and don't brush your teeth, you will probably get toothache sooner or later.

examples.normal: The doctor sees more than twenty patients every morning.
examples.hard: The nurses at this hospital are very kind and always take time to talk to their patients.

examples.easy: Junk food is bad for you.

examples.hard: If you want to lose weight, you should stop eating junk food and start cooking fresh meals at home.

examples.normal: Please keep the milk in the fridge so it stays fresh.
examples.hard: You should keep all your receipts for at least a year in case you need to return something.

examples.normal: Drink hot tea with honey if you have a sore throat.
examples.hard: She had a sore throat and a high temperature, so she stayed in bed and called the doctor.

examples.normal: Don't throw rubbish on the street; use the bin instead.
examples.hard: The rubbish is collected every Tuesday morning, so we put the bins outside on Monday night.

examples.normal: According to the timetable, the next train leaves at six.
examples.hard: At the start of each term, students get a new timetable showing all their lessons and teachers.

examples.normal: I don't think he is telling us the whole truth.
examples.hard: It took the police several months to find out the truth about what happened on that night.

examples.normal: The weather was perfect for a picnic in the park.
examples.hard: Nobody is perfect, so don't worry too much if you make a few mistakes in your presentation.

units.name: Lesson 24 - The past, dates and life events

examples.normal: What will the weather be like at the weekend?
examples.hard: If the weather is good tomorrow, we're going to have a barbecue in the garden with our neighbours.

examples.normal: He was absent from work for a week because of flu.
examples.hard: If you are absent from more than three lessons, you must bring a note from your doctor.

examples.normal: The banks are shut on Sunday, so I'll go on Monday.
examples.hard: She shut all the windows before she went out, because the forecast said there would be a storm.

examples.normal: In the past, people didn't have mobile phones or the internet.
examples.hard: My grandmother loves talking about the past and the village where she grew up after the war.

examples.normal: Please don't use the office computer for personal emails.
examples.hard: She doesn't like talking about her personal life at work, so we know very little about her family.

examples.easy: He wants to be a politician.
examples.normal: Many people don't believe what politicians say on television.
examples.hard: The young politician promised to build new schools and hospitals if people voted for him in the election.

examples.normal: I asked the shop assistant if they had this jacket in blue.
examples.hard: She worked as a shop assistant in a bookshop while she was studying at university.

examples.normal: Our flight landed in Tashkent at six o'clock in the morning.
examples.hard: Because of the heavy snow, the plane couldn't land in Moscow and had to fly to another city.

examples.normal: We sat outside and looked at the full moon last night.
examples.hard: In 1969, Neil Armstrong became the first person to walk on the moon, and millions watched it on TV.

examples.easy: My grandfather fought in the war.
examples.normal: Many buildings in the old town were destroyed during the war.
examples.hard: After the war ended in 1945, many families moved to the cities to look for work and a new life.

examples.normal: Come on, hurry up! The bus is leaving in two minutes.
examples.hard: Come on, you can do it, just one more kilometre and you'll finish the race!

examples.normal: Two men robbed a jewellery shop in the city centre yesterday.
examples.hard: He was robbed on his way home from work, and the thieves took his phone, his wallet and his watch.

examples.normal: She doesn't work at the hospital anymore; she's retired now.
examples.hard: We don't go to that restaurant anymore because the food got worse and the prices went up.

examples.normal: The main character in the book is a young doctor in London.
examples.hard: I didn't enjoy the film because the characters weren't interesting and the story was hard to follow.

examples.normal: Turn off the TV so you can focus on your homework.
examples.hard: This year the company is going to focus on selling its products online instead of opening new shops.

examples.normal: Always compare prices before you buy a new phone online.
examples.hard: If you compare life now with life fifty years ago, you'll see how much technology has changed everything.

examples.normal: We had a big family celebration for my grandmother's eightieth birthday.
examples.hard: The New Year celebrations in the city centre included fireworks, live music and dancing until two in the morning.

examples.normal: We use ordinals like 'first' and 'second' to say dates.
examples.hard: In English, most ordinals end in '-th', but 'first', 'second' and 'third' are irregular.
